classification.difficultyReason: Derive two unknown y-intercepts from the supplied points, then identify a perpendicular base and height to calculate the triangle's area.

spec.description: Two ungridded coordinate lines with double-ended arrows, labelled points and axes. Blue identifies k and red identifies l; all labels and axes are black.
spec.mathematics: Line k passes through A(4,-1) and (6,-6). Line l passes through A(4,-1) and (8,2). B and C are their respective y-intercepts. No intercept coordinates are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; derived intercepts and area remain in the answers.

answer.worked:
For line $k$:
$$\begin{align*}m_k&=\frac{-6-(-1)}{6-4}\\m_k&=-\frac52\\y&=-\frac52x+c\\-1&=-\frac52(4)+c\\c&=9\end{align*}$$
Thus $B=(0,9)$.

For line $l$:
$$\begin{align*}m_l&=\frac{2-(-1)}{8-4}\\m_l&=\frac34\\y&=\frac34x+c\\-1&=\frac34(4)+c\\c&=-4\end{align*}$$
Thus $C=(0,-4)$. The base $BC$ lies on the $y$-axis, so the perpendicular height from $A$ is $4$ units.
$$\begin{align*}BC&=9-(-4)\\BC&=13\\\text{Area}&=\frac12\times13\times4\\\text{Area}&=26\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
For line $k$:
$$\begin{align*}m_k&=\frac{3-2}{-5-(-10)}\\m_k&=\frac15\\y&=\frac15x+c\\2&=\frac15(-10)+c\\c&=4\end{align*}$$
Thus $B=(0,4)$.

For line $l$:
$$\begin{align*}m_l&=\frac{0-2}{-6-(-10)}\\m_l&=-\frac12\\y&=-\frac12x+c\\0&=-\frac12(-6)+c\\c&=-3\end{align*}$$
Thus $C=(0,-3)$. The base $BC$ lies on the $y$-axis, so the perpendicular height from $A$ is $10$ units.
$$\begin{align*}BC&=4-(-3)\\BC&=7\\\text{Area}&=\frac12\times7\times10\\\text{Area}&=35\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$
